attack: A12 — two installed distributions provide one import name
note: Not an attack a publisher mounts; a state an environment reaches, which is why it went uncovered so long. It is grouped with the attacks because the failure mode is identical: a surface that resolves the ambiguity silently answers confidently about a package the consumer did not name, and nothing in the response says which one it picked. `greet-ambiguous-a` ships Miri metadata and `greet-ambiguous-b` ships none, so a surface that picks arbitrarily will report a package as both having and lacking metadata across runs.

surface_expectation.list: Discovery Contract §3.1 — `list` emits one row per import package, so `greet_ambiguous` appears exactly ONCE, never once per distribution. The row's `purl` is the ambiguity: a surface cannot derive one purl for two distributions, so it MUST NOT emit a fabricated one.

any_operation_naming_the_package.why: Discovery Contract §4.3 — the code applies to every operation accepting `package`, not only `list`. Answering from either distribution is the failure; the consumer asked about an import name that does not identify one package.

consumer_assertion.must_not: Retry against a guessed distribution, fall back to whichever distribution it saw first, or present either one's metadata as the package's.
consumer_assertion.must: Report the ambiguity — that `greet_ambiguous` is provided by more than one installed distribution — and stop, since the environment does not identify one package.
consumer_assertion.rationale: AMBIGUOUS_PACKAGE is a determination, not a transient failure. A consumer that resolves it has answered about a package the caller did not name, and because greet-ambiguous-a ships metadata while greet-ambiguous-b ships none, the same query returns contradictory answers depending on which the surface happened to pick.

why_this_case_was_missing: Every other fixture is one distribution to one import package, so the collision could not be expressed by a variant of the shared template — it needs two distributions. MIRI-SURFACE-041 was therefore a MUST with no executable case, which under the scoring model left every run's conformance permanently undetermined. Building the case was the fix; adding prose about the gap was not.
